1	"""Monte Carlo corner analysis for link budgets and circuit metrics.
2	
3	Photonics has no CMOS-grade statistical corner models; the practical
4	substitute is transparent Monte Carlo over declared parameter variations.
5	This module runs any scalar metric (link margin, insertion loss, Q, ...)
6	over sampled process/environment corners and reports distribution statistics
7	and parametric yield.
8	
9	Typical use::
10	
11	    params = [
12	        Normal("gc_loss_db", mean=1.75, sigma=0.25, low=0.0),
13	        Uniform("laser_power_dbm", low=11.0, high=13.0),
14	    ]
15	
16	    def margin(p):
17	        link = make_link(gc=p["gc_loss_db"], laser=p["laser_power_dbm"])
18	        return link.margin_db
19	
20	    result = run(margin, params, n=10_000, seed=1)
21	    print(result.report(threshold=0.0))
22	
23	Module-level (max-of-N) yield
24	-----------------------------
25	A co-packaged-optics module carries N parallel lanes and is scrapped if any
26	single lane misses spec, so module yield is P(ALL lanes pass) — not the
27	per-lane yield. Within one die the variation is mostly common-mode (all
28	lanes shift together with lithography, film thickness, temperature) with a
29	smaller lane-to-lane differential spread; :class:`CommonDifferential`
30	models that split and :func:`run_module` propagates it to lane and module
31	yield. The gap between the two IS the known-good-die problem.
32	
33	All of this is architecture-level statistics over declared variations, not
34	foundry-calibrated signoff: use it to size margins and lane counts, not to
35	predict absolute yield of a specific process.
36	"""
37	
38	from __future__ import annotations
39	
40	from collections.abc import Callable, Sequence
41	from dataclasses import dataclass
42	
43	import numpy as np
44	
45	
46	@dataclass(frozen=True)
47	class Normal:
48	    """Normally distributed parameter, optionally truncated to [low, high].
49	
50	    Truncation is by resampling, so the realized distribution is the exact
51	    truncated normal (no clipping mass at the bounds).
52	    """
53	
54	    name: str
55	    mean: float
56	    sigma: float
57	    low: float | None = None
58	    high: float | None = None
59	
60	    def __post_init__(self):
61	        if self.sigma < 0:
62	            raise ValueError("sigma must be >= 0")
63	        if self.low is not None and self.high is not None and self.low >= self.high:
64	            raise ValueError("low must be < high")
65	
66	    def sample(self, n: int, rng: np.random.Generator) -> np.ndarray:
67	        x = rng.normal(self.mean, self.sigma, n)
68	        lo = -np.inf if self.low is None else self.low
69	        hi = np.inf if self.high is None else self.high
70	        for _ in range(1000):
71	            bad = (x < lo) | (x > hi)
72	            if not bad.any():
73	                return x
74	            x[bad] = rng.normal(self.mean, self.sigma, int(bad.sum()))
75	        raise ValueError(f"{self.name}: truncation bounds reject nearly all samples")
76	
77	
78	@dataclass(frozen=True)
79	class Uniform:
80	    """Uniformly distributed parameter on [low, high]."""
81	
82	    name: str
83	    low: float
84	    high: float
85	
86	    def __post_init__(self):
87	        if self.low >= self.high:
88	            raise ValueError("low must be < high")
89	
90	    def sample(self, n: int, rng: np.random.Generator) -> np.ndarray:
91	        return rng.uniform(self.low, self.high, n)
92	
93	
94	Param = Normal | Uniform
95	
96	
97	@dataclass(frozen=True)
98	class CommonDifferential:
99	    """Parameter with a shared common-mode part and a per-lane differential part.
100	
101	    Models within-die variation of an N-lane module: one common draw
102	    ``common ~ N(0, sigma_common)`` is shared by every lane of a module
103	    (lithography, film thickness, die temperature move all lanes together),
104	    and each lane adds an independent ``diff ~ N(0, sigma_diff)``::
105	
106	        value[trial, lane] = mean + common[trial] + diff[trial, lane]
107	
108	    so the marginal of each lane is N(mean, sqrt(sigma_common^2 +
109	    sigma_diff^2)) and the correlation between two lanes of the same module
110	    is sigma_common^2 / (sigma_common^2 + sigma_diff^2). Units are whatever
111	    the named parameter uses (dB, um, nm, ...).
112	
113	    Optional ``low``/``high`` truncate the TOTAL value by resampling (like
114	    :class:`Normal`, no clipping mass at the bounds). Truncation is
115	    hierarchical to preserve the shared common mode: the common draw is
116	    first resampled until ``mean + common`` lies in [low, high], then each
117	    offending lane's differential draw is resampled until its total does.
118	    In the ``sigma_diff = 0`` limit this is the exact truncated normal; with
119	    ``sigma_diff > 0`` the total's marginal is close to, but not exactly,
120	    the truncated N(mean, sqrt(sigma_common^2 + sigma_diff^2)).
121	    """
122	
123	    mean: float
124	    sigma_common: float
125	    sigma_diff: float
126	    low: float | None = None
127	    high: float | None = None
128	
129	    def __post_init__(self):
130	        if self.sigma_common < 0:
131	            raise ValueError("sigma_common must be >= 0")
132	        if self.sigma_diff < 0:
133	            raise ValueError("sigma_diff must be >= 0")
134	        if self.low is not None and self.high is not None and self.low >= self.high:
135	            raise ValueError("low must be < high")
136	
137	    def sample(self, n_modules: int, n_lanes: int, rng: np.random.Generator) -> np.ndarray:
138	        """Draw a (n_modules, n_lanes) array with one common draw per module."""
139	        lo = -np.inf if self.low is None else self.low
140	        hi = np.inf if self.high is None else self.high
141	        common = rng.normal(0.0, self.sigma_common, n_modules)
142	        if self.low is not None or self.high is not None:
143	            for _ in range(1000):
144	                bad = (self.mean + common < lo) | (self.mean + common > hi)
145	                if not bad.any():
146	                    break
147	                common[bad] = rng.normal(0.0, self.sigma_common, int(bad.sum()))
148	            else:
149	                raise ValueError(
150	                    "CommonDifferential: truncation bounds reject nearly all samples"
151	                )
152	        x = self.mean + common[:, None] + rng.normal(0.0, self.sigma_diff, (n_modules, n_lanes))
153	        for _ in range(1000):
154	            bad = (x < lo) | (x > hi)
155	            if not bad.any():
156	                return x
157	            center = np.broadcast_to(self.mean + common[:, None], x.shape)[bad]
158	            x[bad] = center + rng.normal(0.0, self.sigma_diff, int(bad.sum()))
159	        raise ValueError("CommonDifferential: truncation bounds reject nearly all samples")
160	
161	
162	ModuleParam = CommonDifferential | Normal | Uniform
163	
164	
165	@dataclass
166	class MonteCarloResult:
167	    """Samples and statistics of one scalar metric over parameter corners."""
168	
169	    metric_name: str
170	    samples: np.ndarray  # shape (n,)
171	    param_samples: dict[str, np.ndarray]
172	
173	    @property
174	    def n(self) -> int:
175	        return self.samples.size
176	
177	    @property
178	    def n_failed(self) -> int:
179	        """Corners where the metric raised (recorded as NaN)."""
180	        return int(np.isnan(self.samples).sum())
181	
182	    @property
183	    def mean(self) -> float:
184	        return float(np.nanmean(self.samples))
185	
186	    @property
187	    def std(self) -> float:
188	        ok = self.n - self.n_failed
189	        return float(np.nanstd(self.samples, ddof=1)) if ok > 1 else 0.0
190	
191	    def percentile(self, p) -> float:
192	        return float(np.nanpercentile(self.samples, p))
193	
194	    def yield_above(self, threshold: float) -> float:
195	        """Fraction of samples with metric > threshold (parametric yield)."""
196	        return float(np.mean(self.samples > threshold))
197	
198	    def sensitivity(self) -> dict[str, float]:
199	        """Pearson correlation of each parameter with the metric.
200	
201	        A cheap screening tool: |r| near 1 means the parameter dominates the
202	        metric spread (for near-linear responses). Constant parameters get 0.
203	        """
204	        out: dict[str, float] = {}
205	        ok = ~np.isnan(self.samples)
206	        m = self.samples[ok]
207	        if m.size < 2:
208	            return {name: 0.0 for name in self.param_samples}
209	        ms = m - m.mean()
210	        for name, x in self.param_samples.items():
211	            xs = x[ok] - x[ok].mean()
212	            denom = np.sqrt((xs**2).sum() * (ms**2).sum())
213	            out[name] = float((xs * ms).sum() / denom) if denom > 0 else 0.0
214	        return out
215	
216	    def report(self, threshold: float | None = None, width: int = 50) -> str:
217	        """Plain-text distribution report with an ASCII histogram."""
218	        lines = [
219	            f"Monte Carlo — {self.metric_name}  (n = {self.n})",
220	            "-" * 66,
221	            f"  mean {self.mean:+9.3f}   std {self.std:8.3f}   "
222	            f"P5 {self.percentile(5):+8.3f}   P50 {self.percentile(50):+8.3f}   "
223	            f"P95 {self.percentile(95):+8.3f}",
224	        ]
225	        if threshold is not None:
226	            lines.append(
227	                f"  yield ({self.metric_name} > {threshold:g}): "
228	                f"{100.0 * self.yield_above(threshold):6.2f} %"
229	            )
230	        if self.n_failed:
231	            lines.append(f"  failed corners (metric raised): {self.n_failed}")
232	        counts, edges = np.histogram(self.samples[~np.isnan(self.samples)], bins=20)
233	        peak = counts.max() if counts.max() > 0 else 1
234	        lines.append("")
235	        for c, lo, hi in zip(counts, edges[:-1], edges[1:]):
236	            bar = "#" * max(0, round(width * c / peak))
237	            lines.append(f"  {lo:+9.3f} .. {hi:+9.3f} | {bar}")
238	        sens = sorted(self.sensitivity().items(), key=lambda kv: -abs(kv[1]))
239	        lines.append("")
240	        lines.append("  sensitivity (Pearson r): " + ", ".join(f"{k} {v:+.2f}" for k, v in sens))
241	        return "\n".join(lines)
242	
243	
244	def run(
245	    metric: Callable[[dict[str, float]], float],
246	    params: Sequence[Param],
247	    n: int = 10_000,
248	    seed: int = 0,
249	    metric_name: str = "metric",
250	) -> MonteCarloResult:
251	    """Evaluate ``metric`` over ``n`` sampled corners of ``params``.
252	
253	    ``metric`` receives one dict mapping parameter name -> sampled value and
254	    returns a scalar. Sampling is reproducible for a given seed. Corners where
255	    ``metric`` raises ValueError are recorded as NaN (e.g. a corner where the
256	    RIN penalty is unreachable) and excluded from mean/std/percentiles, but a
257	    failing corner is itself yield-relevant, so NaN counts as a yield loss in
258	    :meth:`MonteCarloResult.yield_above`.
259	    """
260	    if n < 1:
261	        raise ValueError("n must be >= 1")
262	    names = [p.name for p in params]
263	    if len(set(names)) != len(names):
264	        raise ValueError("duplicate parameter names")
265	    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
266	    draws = {p.name: p.sample(n, rng) for p in params}
267	    out = np.empty(n)
268	    for i in range(n):
269	        corner = {name: float(draws[name][i]) for name in names}
270	        try:
271	            out[i] = float(metric(corner))
272	        except ValueError:
273	            out[i] = np.nan
274	    return MonteCarloResult(metric_name=metric_name, samples=out, param_samples=draws)

277	@dataclass
278	class ModuleYieldResult:
279	    """Lane-metric samples and lane vs module yield of an N-lane module.
280	
281	    ``samples[i, j]`` is the metric of lane j in module trial i; a NaN entry
282	    is a lane whose metric raised ValueError — that lane fails every spec,
283	    and with it its module. The difference between :meth:`lane_yield_above`
284	    and :meth:`module_yield_above` is the known-good-die (KGD) problem: with
285	    N lanes per module and any lane-level fallout, module yield collapses
286	    toward lane_yield**N unless the variation is common-mode, which is why
287	    CPO economics hinge on pre-bond lane test and on how much of the spread
288	    is shared across a die.
289	    """
290
